back: First, deep working of the soil that breaks and turns it: ploughing, digging.
Shallower work after ploughing to make the seedbed: harrowing, raking, rolling, ridging.
Control weeds, loosen and aerate soil, bury residues and manure, make a seedbed, expose pests, level or shape land, conserve water.
Survey, slash, fell, stump, remove stones, dispose of debris, build contours, then plough.
Fine, firm and level; large seeds tolerate a medium tilth; tubers need deep, loose soil or ridges.
Only planting lines or basins are disturbed and residues are kept as mulch; zero tillage plants into untilled soil.
Minimum: less erosion, more moisture and organic matter, less fuel; but more weed control and residue-borne pests.
A compacted layer formed by ploughing at the same depth every year; broken with a ripper or subsoiler.
